zh: 好子序列的值互不相同且覆盖 [最小值, 最大值] 的每个整数，所以它的值集合一定是某个整数区间 [l, r]，并且区间里每个值恰好选一个下标；子序列按下标排好后自然唯一，值的先后顺序无关紧要。
设 f[v] 为值 v 的出现次数，固定区间 [l, r] 的方案数就是 f[l]·…·f[r]。按最大值分类更好算：令 end[v] 为最大值恰为 v 的好子序列数，单独选 v 有 f[v] 种，否则是在最大值为 v−1 的好子序列上再添一个 v 的下标，所以 end[v] = f[v]·(1 + end[v−1])；缺失的值 f[v] = 0 会自然把 end 归零。
统计频次后按值从 1 扫到 100000，依次更新 end 并把它累加进答案。答案不取模，最多约 30103 位十进制，必须用任意精度整数：Java 用 BigInteger、Go 用 math/big，C++ 可以自己用 10^9 进制的数组实现“加一、乘小整数、大数相加”三种操作，最后按 9 位补零输出。
en: A good subsequence has distinct values covering every integer between its minimum and maximum, so its value set is an integer range [l, r] with exactly one index chosen for each value in it; once the indices are sorted the subsequence is unique, and the order of the values does not matter.

Let f[v] be the number of occurrences of v; a fixed range [l, r] gives f[l] * ... * f[r] choices. It is easier to group by the maximum: let end[v] be the number of good subsequences whose maximum is v. Choosing v alone gives f[v] ways; otherwise you add one index of v to a good subsequence with maximum v-1, so end[v] = f[v] * (1 + end[v-1]). A missing value has f[v] = 0, which resets end to 0 automatically.

After counting frequencies, scan the values from 1 to 100000, update end and add it to the answer. The answer is not reduced by any modulus and can have about 30103 decimal digits, so arbitrary-precision integers are required: BigInteger in Java, math/big in Go, and in C++ a hand-written base-10^9 limb array supporting add one, multiply by a small integer, and big addition, printed with each lower limb padded to 9 digits.

explanationEn:
## Fixed source and the exact-integer convention

fastprep/Flexport/flexport-count-good-subsequences.md at the fixed commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc fully specifies: 1<=n<=100000 and 1<=arr[i]<=100000; the values in a good subsequence are distinct, and every integer between the minimum and the maximum appears. Counting is by the chosen indices: different indices are counted separately even if they produce the same value sequence. A subsequence keeps the original index order, but its values need not be ascending. A good sequence needs a minimum and a maximum, so the empty sequence is not counted.

The raw return description and the starter code say long, but over the full range 64 bits are not enough: with each of the values 1 to 64 appearing twice, an array of only 128 elements already has the answer 73786976294838206332. The three-language code in the same fixed MDX additionally applies modulo 1000000007, which neither the body text nor raw specifies. This site keeps the complete mathematical counting rule and explicitly outputs the exact decimal integer: no modulus, no truncation, and no shrinking of the input domain to fit long. This is an explicit correction of the overly narrow interface and of the curated code; it does not claim that the original platform guaranteed arbitrary precision. No upstream code was executed.

The original snapshot has no formal input/output examples. All three public examples are marked as derived by this site: for the array [2,2,1], the three single-element index choices plus two choices containing both 1 and 2 give 5 in total; for [1,3], only single elements can be chosen, 2 in total; for [3,1,2], the three single elements, one each for the value ranges [1,2] and [2,3], and all three elements give 6 in total. This site's standard input is n followed by n numbers, and the output is the exact integer.

## Approach

Let f[v] be the number of occurrences of value v. The value set of a good subsequence must be some integer range [l,r], with exactly one index chosen for each value. For a fixed range the index choices of the values are independent, so there are f[l]*...*f[r] ways. Sorting the chosen indices automatically yields the unique subsequence that keeps the original order, and the chosen values need not be ascending.

Let end[v] be the number of good subsequences whose maximum is v. The single-value set {v} has f[v] ways; every other set is obtained from a good subsequence with maximum v-1 by adding one index of value v, so end[v]=f[v]*(1+end[v-1]). Scan the values from small to large and add up end. A missing value with f[v]=0 sets end to zero, which naturally cuts off non-contiguous ranges.

## Proof of correctness

Every good subsequence has a unique minimum l and maximum r. Distinct values together with range coverage guarantee that it takes exactly one index from each value of [l,r]. Conversely, any such choice of indices, ordered by index, forms a good subsequence, and different choices differ in at least one index. So the product count for a fixed range counts everything once and only once.

The valid sets with maximum v split into the single value {v} and ranges of length at least 2. The former contributes f[v]; for the latter, deleting the unique v gives a valid index set with maximum v-1. Adding any one index of value v to such a set and ordering by index exactly reverses the deletion, a one-to-one correspondence. Hence the recurrence is correct. Sets with different maxima are disjoint, and adding up all end values gives all non-empty good subsequences, so the reference program outputs the exact answer.

## Complexity and big integers

Let V=100000. Counting frequencies is O(n); the scan performs O(V) big-integer additions and multiplications by small integers of at most n; big-integer arithmetic cannot unconditionally be treated as constant time. The answer is at most the number of non-empty index subsets, 2^n-1, so every accumulated value has at most n binary digits, at most 30103 decimal digits. Counting bit operations, a conservative upper bound is O(n+V*n*log(n+1)), with space for O(n+V) input/frequency values plus O(n)-bit big integers; in this domain the actual multipliers occupy a single machine word, far less than general big-integer multiplication. Decimal conversion is extra, and multiple-precision libraries may use superlinear algorithms, but the full-domain output is only about 30KB.

Python uses arbitrary-precision integers and lifts the default 4300-digit decimal conversion limit of newer versions with sys.set_int_max_str_digits(0); this is legitimate data that must be handled, not abnormal input. Java can use BigInteger, Go can use math/big, and C++ can use boost::multiprecision::cpp_int; none of them may replace the count with floating point.

## Independent validation

The 163 unique small inputs are checked by directly enumerating all non-empty index subsets and testing each for distinct values and max-min+1 equal to the subset size, without the frequency recurrence. Medium scale uses an independent oracle that explicitly enumerates all value ranges and multiplies item by item. The full scale covers all-equal values, all-distinct values, reverse order, gaps, each value repeated 2/3/4 times, shuffled order, and non-uniform frequencies.

When r consecutive values each appear q times, grouping by range length L gives the answer sum of (r-L+1)*q^L. For q=1 it is r(r+1)/2; for q>1 the closed form is (q^(r+2)-(r+1)*q^2+r*q)/(q-1)^2. With 33333 consecutive values each appearing 3 times, plus the next value once, the answer is this closed form plus 1+3*(3^33333-1)/2, 15905 digits in total. The formal expected outputs are stored as decimal strings to avoid JSON number rounding. The two negative controls wrongly add a modulus and wrongly deduplicate by value, respectively; each counts as a valid kill only after exiting normally on all formal inputs.
